dataset: NREL End-Use Load Profiles for the U.S. Building Stock (ResStock)
weather_note: Actual Meteorological Year 2018 (real July 2018 weather). tmy3 is ruled out: bldg 1 under resstock_tmy3_release_2 gives week-sums 137.338 / 46.072, not 150.245 / 50.099.
local_derivation: One-week slice (2018-07-15 00:15 .. 2018-07-22 00:00, 672 rows, 15-min end-of-interval) of the six out.electricity HVAC columns from the source per-building timeseries, re-saved via pandas.to_parquet. The original ResStock DatetimeIndex and key/value metadata were not preserved, which is why this provenance had to be recovered by fingerprint rather than read from the file.
timezone: US Central Standard Time (UTC-6), no DST (ResStock local-standard-time convention)
recovered_by: Fingerprint match against the OEDI data lake: building_id / upgrade / release / weather were not recorded in the original file. Matched cooling and cooling_fans week-sums to full precision against the amy2018 release_2 AL by-state timeseries; tmy3 ruled out.
caveats: Weather year is amy2018, so this HVAC load is actual July 2018 meteorology. carbon_sim.py re-dates it +364 days to July 2019 (REDATE) to meet the 2019 EIA carbon series -- a cross-year join (2018 weather priced against 2019 grid carbon), disclosed in carbon_sim.py's module docstring.

This local file is a one-week summer slice. A full-year run needs the full source timeseries: heating is 0 here only because July has no electric heating; winter would be non-zero, which is exactly the seasonality gap behind the 'heating and cooling' phrasing.
